results.title: Higman–Neumann–Neumann embedding theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every countable group $G$ embeds in a group generated by two elements: there are a group $H$, elements $a, b \in H$ that generate $H$, and an injective group homomorphism $f \colon G \to H$.

results.title: Infinite finitely presented simple groups exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a natural number $n$ and a finite set $R$ of elements of the free group on generators $x_1, \dots, x_n$ such that the group $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ presented by these generators and relators is simple and infinite.

results.title: SQ-universal group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is SQ-universal if every countable group is isomorphic to a subgroup of a quotient of $G$: for every countable group $C$ there are a group $Q$, a surjective homomorphism $G \to Q$ and an injective homomorphism $C \to Q$.

results.title: The Baumslag–Solitar group BS(1, n)
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{BS}(1, n)$ is the group with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b a b^{-1} = a^n \rangle$.

results.title: Separable subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is separable when for every element $x \in G$ with $x \notin H$ there are a finite group $F$ and a group homomorphism $f \colon G \to F$ with $f(x) \notin f(H)$.

results.title: Locally subgroup-separable (LERF) group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is locally subgroup-separable, or LERF, when every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is separable.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.2 (R. C. Alperin)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finitely generated solvable group $G$ is locally subgroup-separable if and only if there is no $n > 1$ such that $G$ has a subgroup isomorphic to the Baumslag–Solitar group $\mathrm{BS}(1, n)$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.2 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finitely generated solvable group $G$ for which the following two conditions are not equivalent: $G$ is locally subgroup-separable; there is no $n > 1$ such that $G$ has a subgroup isomorphic to the Baumslag–Solitar group $\mathrm{BS}(1, n)$.

results.title: Caprace's class $\mathcal{S}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ with a topology belongs to the class $\mathcal{S}$ when it is a topological group that is Hausdorff, totally disconnected, locally compact and not discrete, is generated as a group by some compact subset, and is topologically simple: $G$ is nontrivial and its only closed normal subgroups are the trivial subgroup and $G$ itself.

results.title: Locally isomorphic topological groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two topological groups are locally isomorphic: they contain open subgroups that are isomorphic as topological groups.

results.title: Caprace's problem on local isomorphism classes (Kourovka 19.22)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that the groups in Caprace's class $\mathcal{S}$ fall into uncountably many local isomorphism classes: there is a family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ of groups in $\mathcal{S}$, indexed by an uncountable set $I$, such that $G_i$ and $G_j$ are not locally isomorphic whenever $i \ne j$.

results.title: Uncountably many local isomorphism classes of simple tdlc groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ of groups in Caprace's class $\mathcal{S}$ (non-discrete, compactly generated, topologically simple, totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff topological groups), indexed by an uncountable set $I$, such that $G_i$ and $G_j$ are not locally isomorphic whenever $i \ne j$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 19.22 (P.-E. Caprace) in the affirmative.

results.title: Irreducible polynomials are expansions of separable irreducibles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero) and let $f \in K[x]$ be irreducible. Then there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and an irreducible separable polynomial $g \in K[x]$ such that $f(x) = g(x^{p^n})$, where $0^0 = 1$.

results.title: The separable irreducible underlying an irreducible polynomial is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero) and let $f \in K[x]$ be irreducible. If $n_1, n_2 \in \mathbb{N}$ and irreducible separable polynomials $g_1, g_2 \in K[x]$ satisfy $f(x) = g_1(x^{p^{n_1}})$ and $f(x) = g_2(x^{p^{n_2}})$, where $0^0 = 1$, then $n_1 = n_2$ and $g_1 = g_2$.

results.title: Irreducible polynomials are uniquely expansions of separable irreducibles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero, and $0^0 = 1$) and let $f \in K[x]$ be irreducible. Then there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and an irreducible separable polynomial $g \in K[x]$ with $f(x) = g(x^{p^n})$, and for every $n' \in \mathbb{N}$ and every irreducible separable polynomial $g' \in K[x]$ with $f(x) = g'(x^{p^{n'}})$ we have $n' = n$ and $g' = g$.

results.title: Number of Hurwitz quaternions of a given norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Hurwitz quaternion is a quaternion $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$ whose rational coordinates $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3$ are either all integers or all halves of odd integers, and its norm is $\mathrm{Nm}(q) = x_0^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2$. For every positive integer $N$, the number of Hurwitz quaternions of norm $N$ is $24 \sum_{d \mid N,\ d \text{ odd}} d$, that is, $24$ times the sum of the odd divisors of $N$.

results.title: Tarski's Euclidean axiom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a model $M$ of Tarski's absolute plane geometry with betweenness relation $B$, where $B(a, b, c)$ means that $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$ (allowing $b = a$ or $b = c$), the Euclidean axiom A10 holds in $M$ when for all points $a, b, c, d, t$ of $M$ with $B(a, d, t)$, $B(b, d, c)$ and $a \ne d$ there are points $x$ and $y$ of $M$ with $B(a, b, x)$, $B(a, c, y)$ and $B(x, t, y)$.

results.title: Independence of the parallel postulate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Tarski's Euclidean axiom A10 is independent of Tarski's axioms of absolute plane geometry: there is a model of absolute plane geometry in which the Euclidean axiom holds, and there is a model of absolute plane geometry in which it fails.

results.title: Almost complex structure on a subset of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ and let $J$ assign to each point $y \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ a real linear map $J(y) : \mathbb{R}^{2n} \to \mathbb{R}^{2n}$. Then $J$ is an almost complex structure on $U$ if $J$ is $C^\infty$ on $U$ and $J(x)(J(x)v) = -v$ for every $x \in U$ and every $v \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

results.title: Revenue of a rod composition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ be a price vector with entries in an additive commutative monoid, where $p_{\ell - 1}$ is the price of a piece of length $\ell$. For $k \le n$ and a composition $(b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of $k$ into positive parts, its revenue is $p_{b_1 - 1} + \dots + p_{b_m - 1}$, the total price of its pieces.

results.title: The empty rod earns nothing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ be prices in an additive commutative monoid. Every composition of $0$, namely the empty one, has revenue $0$ with respect to $p$.

results.title: Revenue of an uncut rod
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ be prices in an additive commutative monoid, $p_i$ being the price of a piece of length $i$. For $0 < k \le n$, the revenue of the one-part composition $(k)$ of $k$ is $p_k$.

results.title: Revenue is additive under concatenation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ be prices in an additive commutative monoid, and define the revenue of a composition $(b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of some $k \le n$ to be $p_{b_1} + \dots + p_{b_m}$. If $c$ is a composition of $k$ and $d$ is a composition of $l$ with $k + l \le n$, then the revenue of their concatenation, a composition of $k + l$, is the revenue of $c$ plus the revenue of $d$.

results.title: Bottom-up rod cutting on the empty rod
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the empty price vector ($n = 0$) over an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, bottom-up rod cutting returns $0$ at cost $0$.

results.title: Cost of bottom-up rod cutting as a sum over rows
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For prices $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ in an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, the cost of bottom-up rod cutting on $p$ (the number of first-piece candidates it evaluates) equals $\sum_{j=0}^{n} j$.

results.title: Twice the cost of bottom-up rod cutting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For prices $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ in an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, the cost $T$ of bottom-up rod cutting on $p$ (the number of first-piece candidates it evaluates) satisfies $2T = n(n + 1)$.

results.title: Exact cost of bottom-up rod cutting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For prices $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ in an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, the cost of bottom-up rod cutting on $p$ (the number of first-piece candidates it evaluates) is the triangular number $n(n + 1)/2$, whatever the prices.

results.title: Bottom-up rod cutting takes quadratic time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For prices $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ in an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, the cost $T$ of bottom-up rod cutting on $p$, the number of first-piece candidates it evaluates, satisfies $n^2 \le 2T$ and $T \le n^2$.

results.title: Saved revenues are optimal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a price vector of length $n$ with entries in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid (addition is monotone), and let $r = (r_0, \dots, r_n)$ be the revenue table computed by the extended bottom-up rod-cutting algorithm. For every $j \le n$, $r_j$ is the greatest revenue of a composition of $j$: some composition of $j$ has revenue $r_j$, and every composition of $j$ has revenue at most $r_j$.

results.title: The extended algorithm computes the same revenue
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every price vector of length $n$ with entries in an additive commutative monoid carrying a linear order, the last entry $r_n$ of the revenue table computed by the extended bottom-up rod-cutting algorithm equals the value returned by the bottom-up rod-cutting algorithm.

results.title: Running time of extended bottom-up rod cutting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid with a linear order. For every vector of $n$ prices in $\alpha$, the extended bottom-up rod-cutting algorithm has cost exactly $n(n+1)/2$, whatever the prices are.

results.title: Reconstruction earns the final saved revenue

results.summary: Let $p$ be a price vector of length $n$ with entries in an additive commutative monoid carrying a linear order, and let $r = (r_0, \dots, r_n)$ be the revenue table computed by the extended bottom-up rod-cutting algorithm. The revenue of the composition of $n$ returned by the rod-cutting reconstruction equals $r_n$.

results.title: Rod-cutting reconstruction is optimal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a price vector of length $n$ with entries in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid (addition is monotone). The composition of $n$ returned by the rod-cutting reconstruction has the greatest revenue among all compositions of $n$: its revenue is at least the revenue of every composition of $n$.

results.title: Running time of recursive CUT-ROD
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid with a linear order, and let $p_1, \dots, p_n \in \alpha$ be prices. Recursive CUT-ROD on these prices, which charges one tick per invocation, makes exactly $2^n$ invocations, counting the root call and every call on an empty rod, whatever the prices are.

results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid with a linear order and let $p \in \alpha^n$ be a vector of prices. The memoized cut-rod procedure on $p$ charges exactly $n^2 + 2n + 2$ events, where one event is charged per cache probe, per first-cut candidate, and per cache write.

results.title: f3 statistic as shared drift on a tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With binary loadings, `f3 O A B` is the total drift length of the edges shared by the paths `O–A` and `O–B` (on a tree, the path from `O` to the `A–B` path).

results.title: Outgroup f3 statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Outgroup `f3` (Raghavan et al. 2014): with binary loadings, if the lineage of `O` shares no edge with the lineages of `A` and `B`, then `f3 O A B` is the drift from the outgroup to the root plus the drift shared by `A` and `B`.

results.title: Outgroup f3 ranks populations by shared drift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a fixed outgroup `O` and population `A`, the outgroup `f3` ranks candidates `B` by the drift they share with `A`.

results.title: MixMapper mixed drift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: MixMapper's mixed drift `α² ℓ_a + (1 - α)² ℓ_b + ℓ_c`: the only combination of the terminal drift lengths that enters the `f2` statistics of an admixed population.

results.title: Admixed-branch identity for f2 statistics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The admixed-branch identity (Lipson et al. 2013): if `Mx` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of the endpoints of the edges `a` (below `A`) and `b` (below `B`), followed by drift on `c`, and `A`, `B`, `X` do not use `a`, `b`, `c`, then `f2 Mx X = α f2 A X + (1 - α) f2 B X - α (1 - α) f2 A B + mixedDrift α ℓ_a ℓ_b ℓ_c`.

results.title: Identifiability of the admixture proportion from f2 statistics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Identifiability of the mixture proportion (our formulation): with the split points `A`, `B` given, two references `X₁`, `X₂` satisfying the hypotheses of `f2_admixedBranch` and with different contrasts `f2 A Xᵢ - f2 B Xᵢ` determine `α` from `f2` statistics.

results.title: Mixed drift determined by f2 statistics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Given `α`, the mixed drift is determined by the `f2` statistics of one reference `X`.
